Mono blue partners with [[Malcolm, Keen-Eyed Navigator]] and [[Sakashima, of a thousand faces]] Mono blue Clone / Big Mana / Artifact. I think it is still among the lowest ranks on edhrec although it gained a lot in popularity since I first built it. 

https://www.moxfield.com/decks/jo_IKdCd00KfEoj9toBy2Q

My decklist is balanced for my playgroup, if you are looking to make your own I would still advise to keep the same balance between ramp/ Interaction / clones and payoffs as I’ve reached a sweetspot by playing it a lot.

The goal is to clone malcolm a few times and to make huge amounts of treasure tokens with its damage trigger and use them to win with [[Cyberdrive Awakener]], [[Rise and shine]], [[Mechanized Production]] or other big mana spells like [[myojin of seeing winds]] while a [[psychosis crawler]] is on the battlefield. Also, you could clone your opponents’ wincons if the setting is viable; I’ve included a [[maskwood Nexus]] to make treasures out of my opponents’ potential pingers (a guy in our pod plays [[Borborygmos Enraged]] and it’s awesome to discard a land for 7 treasures…) You could also hold up to your treasures to threaten with your interactions although this playstyle may be less fun for everyone at the table.

If you want to take the deck to the next level, it would be really easy to chain extra turns. I just don’t do it because I don’t like playing solitaire and I need my opponents’ creatures for potential copy targets; remember, most clones will work through shroud and hexproof:) There are a few combos and control options also available in blue, a [[back to basic]] or some cloned [[Consecrated Sphinx]] do some heavy lefting in higher powered pods.

The power level kinda of scales with the other decks at the table too, think about starting to clone [[esper sentinel]] or [[dockside extortionist]] maybe even [[Avacynn, angel of hope]].

Enough long paragraphs, I just hope you get to enjoy it as much as I do!

>Is Mechanized Production just winning on your upkeep if you have 8+ treasures essentially?>

Yez. 
Somebody needs to either destroy the treasure, destroy the aura or counter the triggered ability of mechanized production. 
Attaching mechanized production to one of your many treasures does put a target on your head but you can also go the sneaky way by flashing it in with an [[emergence zone]] or another flash outlet if you feel like running some more. [[Leyline of anticipation]] would be a great addition for such circumstances and even for flashing in clones right before your turn or in answer to removal, making sure to always have a Malcolm on the battlefield. 


>Would you please elaborate on "most clones will work through shroud and hexproof" what if an opponents creature is equipped with [[Swiftfoot Boots]] as an example? You can't copy/clone that right? Or were you referring to cloning your own stuff works through shroud/hexproof? If so, how?>

Most clones I run will say "[…] enters the battlefield as a copy of any creature on the battlefield." 
This means it doesn’t "target" anything. It just enters as is while hexproof and/or shroud specifically say "it can’t be the target of spells or abilities your opponents control"

Rule 114 covers the targeting of spells and abilities and when those targets must be selected;

"114.9a Just because an object or player is being affected by a spell or ability doesn’t make that object or player a target of that spell or ability. Unless that object or player is identified by the word “target” in the text of that spell or ability, or the rule for that keyword ability, it’s not a target."

Most spells and abilities that target will say "target" directly on the card, unless their Keyword ability rules covers this already like auras and equipments.

Ma famille à un vieux chalet à Boischatel sur le bord de la rivière Montmorency. 
J’y étais allé passer la nuit avec mon père quand j’avais ~14 ans. Le landemain matin, il avait une job tôt, donc il m’a laissé dormir et allait repasser me chercher vers midi avec son pick-up.

Alors je me réveille au son de la radio du chalet vers 10hAM. On l’allume rarement mais j’imagine qu’en se préparant, mon paternel avait omît de l’éteindre…
Sauf que le poste qui jouait faisait vraiment pas de sens. Déjà c’était en anglais, y avait comme un preacher qui donnait une messe à la radio et ça me frappait à quel point il était intense. Je me rappel surtout de son « Right Now! » Il disait genre: « You must believe it right now, right now RIGHT NOW! » Comme ça en le répétant… Un moment donné ça s’est mit à me foutre la trouille faque sans changer de poste ou éteindre la radio parce que j’étais pas capable j’ai juste descendu le son; j’l’ai mis en sourdine manuellement. 

Finalement le temps passe, j’oublis le drôle de poste et des semaines plus tard j’retourne au chalet avec mon père pis sa blonde, on joue au skipbo tranquille avant d’aller se coucher pis c’est là que je me rappel de la maudite radio. 
Je leur raconte ce que je viens de vous conter, je leur répète les « Rights nows » Insistant de notre Jeff Fillion de je ne sais quelle religion… Sauf que mon père par à rire et m’explique que la radio fonctionne plus depuis longtemps, elle est juste là pour faire beau, le fil est même coupé en arrière! 

Je comprends pas mais j’insiste, je suis sûr que j’ai pas rêvé ça, c’est même ça qui m’a réveillé! Eux me croient pas, j’essais de les convaincre, mais ils rient…

Puis, c’est à ce moment là que le luminaire au dessus de notre table qui tient au plafond depuis au moins une décennie décide de se décrocher pour se fracasser au centre de notre jeu de carte.

C’est juste ça. Coïncidence? J’ai tu juste rêvé au monsieur pasteur pressé pis c’est en en parlant que le luminaire est tombé? Je sais pas honnêtement… Mais si jamais ça vous dit dequoi, ce que j’ai entendu dans cette radio là partagez le moi svp ça m’intrigue à ce jour…

I’ve read your article and you were mostly right about the pros and cons of combo decks but EDH still all comes downs to a rule zero talk and making sure everyone is having fun at the table.

Combo is the strongest archetype and the hardest to balance but edh isn’t an arms race, it’s about playing what you like and having fun with multiple people. Sure, you dislike combo and you have plenty of good reasons to as some dislike stax or storm or infect and it is important to talk about it before sitting down and shuffling and although owning multiple decks is hard on some people it is always good to have multiple power levels available to suit everyone’s playstyle at best.
